That exact test method is NOT present in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour: it is about `str()`/`repr()` of an rrule object and about an "RRULE" token being appended/emitted. IMPORTANT: another agent may be editing a DIFFERENT part of /dateutil/dateutil/rrule.py at the same time. So: (a) re-read the file right before each edit, (b) keep your edit minimal and localized to the `__str__`/`__repr__` code, (c) if an edit fails because the file changed, re-read and retry, (d) never rewrite the whole file, never use git checkout/reset, and never touch anything outside the __str__/__repr__ area.

Steps:
1. Read /dateutil/dateutil/rrule.py fully (especially __str__, __repr__, and any helper that builds the string), plus /dateutil/dateutil/test/test_rrule.py for existing str/repr tests.
2. Reproduce with python3 -c '...': print(str(rrule(DAILY, count=3, dtstart=datetime(2000,1,1)))), print(repr(...)), print(str(rruleset(...))), print(str(rrule(...))) for several frequencies/options, and compare with what the docstring/docs say.
3. Fix minimally in /dateutil/dateutil/rrule.py ONLY.
4. Verify: run `cd /dateutil && python3 -m pytest dateutil/test/test_rrule.py -q` (fallback `python3 -m unittest dateutil.test.test_rrule -v`) BEFORE and AFTER; no pre-existing passing test may start failing. Note that another agent may be concurrently editing the file, so if you see unrelated failures, re-check whether they pre-exist by testing with `git stash`-free means (do NOT stash): instead just report them.

Constraints: only /dateutil/dateutil/rrule.py may be modified, and only in the __str__/__repr__ area. Do not edit tests. Do not add features. No internet access.

Report back: (a) the exact bug and root cause, (b) the exact diff (file + lines), (c) before/after test results, (d) commands + outputs showing correct str/repr behaviour, (e) any uncertainty.

   python3 -c "from dateutil.parser import parse; print(parse('I have a meeting on 25th of September 2003', fuzzy_with_tokens=True))"
   Try many fuzzy inputs, including ones with leading/trailing junk, times, timezones, and compare to the documented behaviour.
